correctness.rationale: On the specified stationary branch, the dimensionless unnormalized remaining half-line mass is U(y)=R_m(g(y)) in gas because U'=-g and U(infinity)=0. The source flux matching gives U(L)=1; the core has U=q exp(-my) and density mU, so L=log(q)/m and survival is U/q. This proves the three quantile formulas, including their joins. From the endpoints of J_m the gas-regime derivative is (H_m(qs)-H_m(q))/(mq), the exterior derivative is (H_m(qs)+1-m)/(mq), and the core derivative is zero. The first two are negative; hence positive y_q/q decreases strictly, even as log(q)/q initially increases for the width. Coupling by a common uniform survival level gives strict expectations of strictly increasing integrable observables. At q=1 the scaling-factor derivative cancels, leaving the stated s-independent kink; H_m is continuous at m=4 even with a singular spatial gas slope. For coexisting stationary profiles subtract the two quantiles: the difference integrates 1/H_m(u)-1/(mu)>0 from max(1,qs) to q. The endpoint q=m/4 is valid for the explicit gas profile, with a one-sided cusp, not a dynamical stability claim. For strong reset the core agrees identically with Exp(m), and translating the exterior multiplies both mass-one densities by 1/q. For weak reset, H_m(q)exp(-2H_m(q)/m)=q-q^2/m+O(q^3); the inverse of h exp(-2h/m) is a+2a^2/m+O(a^3), uniformly at a=O(q exp(-y)). Dividing by q and integrating the absolute first-order correction yields q/(4m), since integral_0^1 |2u-1|du=1/2. Replay: RESULT.md lines 73–146. As a separate bounded check of the strong coefficient, solve log(h/m)+m[log(H_m(1)/h)-2(H_m(1)-h)/m]=0 for h in (0,H_m(1)) by bisection (the expression tends to +infinity at zero, is negative at H_m(1), and has at most one interior minimum). The density crossing gives Delta_m=h(1-(1+h)/m), yielding 0.378426, 0.472058, 0.676129 and 0.804631 for m=4,5,10,20. The frozen verification code was inspected, not executed.
